items.title: Larry Ridley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 10, 2003
items.q: I mean people in Chicago weren’t waiting on King Oliver to get off the riverboat and say come on in here King Oliver and teach us how to play jazz.

ctx.x: Yeah. That’s — and you know you have the Pettiford family? All these territories. See and that’s another thing that I am very, very adamant about too is this mythology about jazz being born only in New Orleans is a myth. Absolute myth. And I did my homework with Eubie Blake and Garvin Bushell and Doc Cheatham and people like this. And they said wherever there was a significant population of people of African descent they were creating a spontaneous improvised hot music. That’s why you have the Afro-Cuban…
Was there ever lessons learned of things not to do?
